exposure: Gestational weight gain (GWG) category (adequate, inadequate, excessive)
outcome: Gestational weight gain (GWG) category (adequate, inadequate, excessive)
cohort: The study included 220 pregnant women who registered for antenatal care before 13 weeks of gestation at Babcock University Teaching Hospital, Nigeria.
finding: A substantial proportion of women experienced suboptimal gestational weight gain, with inadequate GWG linked to older maternal age, multiparity, higher socioeconomic class, and subsequent reduced risk of caesarean delivery and lower infant birth weight.
mod_finding: Women with inadequate gestational weight gain had a 30% reduced risk of caesarean delivery compared to those with adequate GWG.
